newsitem.title: USA: Boeing names new defense group president.
newsitem.headline: Boeing names new defense group president.

text.p: Boeing Co. said Monday that Alan Mulally, an executive in its commercial airplane group, will become president of the defence and space group effective immediately, succeeding Jerry King.
King, who had planned to retire in mid-1997, has been put in charge of the transition team working on Boeing's planned acquisition of McDonnell Douglas Corp.

Boeing said King would work with a transition steering group comprised of Mulally, commercial airplane group President Ron Woodard, chief financial officer Boyd Givan, and Boeing general counsel Ted Collins.
As one of only three operating division presidents at Boeing, Mulally, 51, takes over a rapidly expanding side of the company's business.

With last year's purchase of some Rockwell International Corp. operations and the pending acquisition of McDonnell Douglas, defence and space will account for an estimated 40 percent of the company's revenues next year, up from less than 30 percent in recent years.

Mulally, previously senior vice president of airplane development and definition in the commercial airplane group, joined Boeing in 1969 and progressed through engineering assignments on every major model.
On the 777 programme he served as vice president of engineering and then as vice president and general manager, overseeing the airplane's initial rollout and first test flight.
King, 61, who joined Boeing as a design engineer, has been with the company since 1958.
"Jerry has provided outstanding leadership to our defence and space Group during the last few, critical years," Boeing Chief Executive officer Phil Condit said in a statement.

"He has left his mark of success on the group for many years to come and will significantly influence transition activities to position the new Boeing for success as the leading integrated aerospace company in the world," Condit said.
Boeing's stock gained $1.625 to end at $106.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
